title: OpenFeature eval context namespace must stay concrete: never '*' or empty from wildcard identities
answers: feature flag evaluation rejected with namespace mismatch for service token
wildcard namespace identity breaks OpenFeature flag evaluation
how is the OpenFeature evaluation context namespace / targeting key chosen per request
cluster-wide service token gets flags evaluated for '*'
body:
Symptom: Requests made with a wildcard identity, such as a cluster-wide service token, had their feature flag evaluations rejected as a namespace mismatch.
Root cause: pkg/services/contexthandler/contexthandler.go:ContextHandler.setRequestContext copied id.Namespace straight into the OpenFeature evaluation context (both the targeting key and the "namespace" attribute). When that value was "*", it no longer matched the caller's concrete auth namespace further down the request path.
Fix pattern: Use the identity namespace only when it is concrete (non-empty and not "*"). Otherwise fall back to "stacks-" + cfg.StackID, and use "default" when StackID is unset. A concrete identity namespace still wins over StackID.
Constraints: Any code that builds an OpenFeature evaluation context, or another per-request scope, from an identity namespace must treat "" and "*" as "no namespace". If it doesn't, the scope widens to wildcard and downstream namespace checks fail. Keep the targeting key and the namespace attribute equal.
applies: OpenFeature evaluation context setup in the request context handler, and any code that derives a namespace from authn identities
